document.title: Senator Brown and Congressman Wilson Discuss Afghanistan with Pakistani Officials
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), The Taliban File
document.note: [Confidential] Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto meets Senator Hank Brown and Congressman Charlie Wilson. She stresses the need for the Trans-Afghan gas pipeline and says the perception that her government backed the Taliban was simply untrue.

mentions.quote: PRIME MINISTER BHUTTO TOLD SENATOR BROWN (R-CO) AND CONGRESSMAN WILSON (D-TX) APRIL 7 THAT THE GOP BACKED THE U.N., NOT THE TALIBAN

persons.name: Hank Brown

mentions.quote: PRIME MINISTER BENAZIR BHUTTO TOLD VISITING SENATOR HANK BROWN AND CONGRESSMAN CHARLIE WILSON OVER LUNCH APRIL 7
CODEL WILSON DEPARTED BEFORE THE MESSAGE WAS PREPARED.
FOREIGN SECRETARY NAJMUDDIN SHAIKH, WHO ALSO ATTENDED THE APRIL 7 LUNCH, SAID NEUTRAL PEACEKEEPERS WOULD BE NECESSARY
FOREIGN MINISTER SARDAR ASSEF ALI TOLD SEN. BROWN IN A SEPARATE MEETING APRIL 7
ASSEF ALI ASKED SEN. BROWN TO CARRY A MESSAGE TO AFGHAN PRESIDENT RABBANI WHEN HE MET HIM APRIL 8.

persons.name: Gulbuddin Hekmatyar
persons.role: Afghan faction leader reconciling with Masood against the Taliban

events.description: Bhutto and Foreign Secretary Shaikh lunch with Sen. Brown and Rep. Wilson; Bhutto denies backing Taliban and pushes pipeline.
Foreign Minister Assef Ali meets Sen. Brown separately, proposes principles for Afghan peace plan and message for Rabbani.
Sen. Brown scheduled to meet Afghan President Rabbani in Kabul, carrying Pakistani message.
US Embassy Islamabad cable reporting the meetings.
Bhutto, with Shaikh, lunched with Brown and Wilson; urged US representation in Kandahar/Jalalabad and pushed the trans-Afghan pipeline.
Assef Ali met Brown separately and proposed US/EU/Russia peace principles.
Brown scheduled to meet Rabbani and convey Pakistan's message.
Embassy Islamabad cable reporting the meetings.
Attack on the Pakistani Embassy in Kabul caused a diplomatic problem.

key_claims: Bhutto publicly denied that Pakistan was backing the Taliban, saying Pakistan supports the UN peace mission.
Pakistan promoted a trans-Afghan gas/oil pipeline as a route for Central Asian energy and a tool for Afghan reconciliation.
Bhutto warned Afghanistan could split into a Taliban Pashtun south and a pro-Iranian minority ethnic north.
Foreign Secretary Shaikh said Hekmatyar and Masood were reconciling for confrontation with the Taliban, not peace.
Pakistan said it would not build a road or pipeline through Afghanistan without Kabul's assent and that only local commanders' agreement and Kabul's passive acquiescence were needed.
Pakistan proposed drafting peace 'principles' with the US, EU and Russia to revive the UN mission of Mestiri.
